Protocol implementation update

Protocol version 2.1 introduces a bounded queue for incoming requests. Each connection has an independent queue, and the server rejects new work when that queue reaches its configured capacity. This prevents one slow client from consuming all of the worker slots available to other clients.

The implementation keeps response buffers until the receiving client acknowledges the corresponding sequence number. A timeout releases those buffers and closes the connection. Operators can adjust the timeout based on observed network latency, while the queue limit remains fixed for the lifetime of each connection.

The protocol documentation describes the message format and the measurements used to choose the default limits.
